transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get started on sprint planning. We've got five candidates on the table for the three platform-debt slots: auth-middleware upgrade, queue-telemetry cleanup, export-pagination work, CI-cache replacement, and log-retention simplification. Before I record the final three-item order, I want to hear from each of you -- backend engineering, site reliability, and customer operations -- on how these candidates look from your side. Who wants to kick things off?

transcript.text: I need to flag something urgent before we go further. This morning, while reviewing a dependency update for an unrelated backend ticket, I confirmed that our current auth-middleware version has a known remotely exploitable vulnerability rated CVSS 8.1. I haven't filed the security ticket yet, but given the severity, the auth-middleware upgrade has to be the first initiative in the sprint.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share something I found during a billing review of our observability usage yesterday. I confirmed that duplicate queue metrics are causing approximately $18,000 per month in avoidable telemetry charges. I'm still validating the billing export, so I haven't posted this in the planning document yet, but given the cost impact, queue-telemetry cleanup must be the second initiative in the sprint.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share something critical from customer operations. While preparing an enterprise renewal brief this afternoon, I confirmed that Northstar's service agreement requires the export API to support paginating 100,000-row results before its renewal review. Export-pagination work is the only candidate that satisfies that requirement, and I haven't yet added the clause to the account record. Given this contractual obligation, export-pagination work must be the third initiative in the sprint.
